text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 30

An all-male panel is common in senior civil service recruitment and, on its own, proves nothing about motive. Leading with it looks speculative and invites the response that the panel was properly constituted. It may be worth noting later as context, not as your main argument.

The real issue is substantive: the stated reason for choosing him was "international project leadership," apparently outweighing your law degree, policy master's and ten years' service. Ask whether that criterion appeared in the published person specification and how it was weighted. If it surfaced only at decision stage, that is a far stronger point.

Chase the written reasons now, in writing, citing the deadline. Non-response is itself a procedural failure.
